items.title: Evan Christopher interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 1, 2009
items.q: unless it was his own quartet, which with the absence of Tony D it was not

ctx.x: I think so. I think so. At the top of his game, yet at the same time I think one of the things that made him a bit maudlin was that he was losing a lot of his own friends: Tony D

[DiNicola] passed away before, just a few months before, the market for the jobs wasn’t getting any better and the quality of the musicians that he was ending up sharing the bandstand with, unless it was his own quartet, which with the absence of Tony D it was not, you know I think things had taken a little bit of a change. So he as an individual may have been feeling really strong and I think he was really, I think he was pretty content in New Mexico. I mean he didn’t like how dry it was but, so yes and no. He…
Well it’s been fascinating talking to you.
